claims.text: Adrahil was the son of Angelimir. He became the twenty-first Prince of Dol Amroth after his father's death in .
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Peoples of Middle-earth, "VII. The Heirs of Elendil", The Line of Dol Amroth, p. 223

claims.text: Adrahil had three children. His oldest daughter, Ivriniel, his second daughter, Finduilas and his youngest child and only son, Imrahil.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Peoples of Middle-earth, "VII. The Heirs of Elendil", genealogical table, p. 221

claims.text: In Adrahil's daughter Finduilas married Denethor, the son of Steward Ecthelion II of Gondor.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, The Lord of the Rings, Appendix B, "The Third Age", entry for the year 2976, p. 1089; J.R.R. Tolkien, The Lord of the Rings, Appendix A, "The Númenorean Kings", "Gondor and the Heirs of Anárion", "The Stewards", entries for Steward Ecthelion II and Steward Denethor II, pp. 1055-56

claims.text: Two years later in Finduilas' older son Boromir was born and five years after that in her younger son Faramir was born.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, The Lord of the Rings, Appendix B, "The Third Age", entries for the years 2978 and 2983, p. 1089

claims.text: Five years after the birth of her second son Faramir, Finduilas died young at the age of 38 in .
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, The Lord of the Rings, Appendix B, "The Third Age", entry for the year 2988, p. 1089

claims.text: Adrahil died in and was succeeded by his only son Imrahil.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Peoples of Middle-earth, "VII. The Heirs of Elendil", The Line of Dol Amroth, p. 223
